editions.text:
October 15 added up to 25 species and 326 feeder visits, both above the past week's averages of 20.1 species and 282.7 visits. By ear, the day logged 394 detections, below the week's average of 423.0. Tufted Titmouse led the visits with 119, followed by Carolina Chickadee with 47.

Thirteen species were recorded on all seven days, including Eastern Phoebe, Eastern Towhee, Northern Cardinal, Carolina Chickadee and Tufted Titmouse, so the regulars held. Several species recorded earlier in the week were not recorded today, among them American Kestrel, Cedar Waxwing, Rose-breasted Grosbeak and American Goldfinch. No species was heard or seen here for the first time, and none was a first confident visual record at this station.

The audio source changed many times during the day, starting at 03:46 and continuing through the morning and evening, with the last change at 21:31. Heard detections for the day therefore come from more than one source, so the lower detection total should not be read as a change in the birds.
